Subject: QuantFlare capacity-basket scenarios and new APAC region ask

Samira —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To make progress on the Dedicated capacity proposal we sketched a couple of regionized capacity "baskets" and need the traffic/SLAs you expect so we can size a recommended commit. Attached: QF_Capacity_Scenarios_v2.xlsx (two baseline scenarios + burst runway).

Quick asks from our side to validate the scenarios:
- Expected 95th percentile token throughput (tokens/sec) and peak concurrency for the first 6 months.
- Typical request distribution by geo (approx % APAC / EU / US). You mentioned APAC is primary — please confirm a % split.
- Latency SLO (95th ms) and acceptable tail for failover to EU/US.
- Any regulatory constraints for APAC region (data residency, KMS requirements).

We sketched two options in the spreadsheet:
- Scenario A (moderate): APAC reserve ~8 A100-eq, EU 4, US 2; autoscale burst lane to 2x for first 90 days.
- Scenario B (aggressive growth): APAC reserve 20 A100-eq, EU 8, US 6; includes standby cold nodes in EU for failover.

If you can provide the 6-month growth curve and procurement timing our pricing team will model committed vs. metered economics. Would a 30-min sync on Friday work to go through numbers?

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Vanessa —

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the spreadsheet. High level numbers from our product team:
- Current steady state: ~1.2M tokens/minute (global) with spikes up to ~3.8M tokens/minute during batch runs.
- Peak concurrency: ~120 concurrent sessions (with async batching for heavy jobs).
- Geo split: APAC ~68%, EU ~18%, US ~14% (APAC-heavy).
- Latency requirement: 95th <= 180ms for interactive requests; batch jobs can be relaxed.

We expect ~30% month-over-month growth for the first 3 months as we ramp. Procurement has asked for a draft SOW and PO template — I've attached a short SOW outline and will loop procurement on pricing once you provide a recommended commit.

Looping Minh on compliance questions (KMS + data residency).

Thanks,

On Wed, Apr 14, 2027 at 11:03 AM Samira Khan <samira@quantflare.ai> wrote:
> High level numbers from our product team:
> - Current steady state: ~1.2M tokens/minute (global) with spikes up to ~3.8M tokens/minute during batch runs.

Thanks — that helps. A few sizing notes from infra/serving perspective:
- Using the numbers provided, Scenario A (moderate) maps to ~7-9 A100-eq GPUs in APAC sustained with headroom; Scenario B (aggressive) looks like 18-24 in APAC. The spreadsheet breaks down token-hours -> GPU-hours by quantization profile.
- Latency: to meet 95th <= 180ms we should pin interactive routing to APAC-reserved capacity and keep EU as warm standby for failover. That means a small EU hot pool (3-4 GPUs) plus a cold buffer for burst.
- Ops ask: we recommend a staged tranche commit: initial 6-month commit (scenario A-min) + optional 3-month burst credits for launch week. This reduces unit pricing while keeping flexibility.
- Suggest enabling int8/4-bit quantization path for generator models (saves ~30-45% GPU-hours depending on model). If QuantFlare is sensitive to quality, we can baseline evals on a representative prompt set.

I've updated the spreadsheet with GPU-hour projections and a suggested tranche structure. Vanessa — can we get procurement's target cadence/lead time so finance can draft a pricing sheet?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
